1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first transmission speed; receiving a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second transmission speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first transmission speed is different from the second transmission speed, and wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status encoded into light pulses as binary bits independent of message transmission speed.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second transmission speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first transmission speed, and wherein the computing device dynamically adjusts the second transmission speed based on proximity and motion characteristics of the vehicle.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on a loss of received light pulse sequences, and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third transmission speed, wherein the third transmission speed is faster than the second transmission speed and is determined based on absence of vehicle proximity signals.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth transmission speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth transmission speed is different from the second transmission speed and is determined independently for each vehicle based on that vehicle's received light pulse sequence characteristics.

5. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth transmission speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth transmission speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles.

11.
